obligations.note: Head commit 6d48175 changes required_approvals from `amount >= policy.DUAL_CONTROL_THRESHOLD` to `amount > ...`. A payment of exactly 10,000.00 now needs only one approver, but PAY-1 requires dual control at or above the approved threshold.

approve() is unchanged and still rejects the creator (SelfApprovalError) and duplicate approvers. is_fully_approved only counts distinct approvers, which can never include the creator, so maker-checker holds at head.

Ticket CHG-25976 is a standard ticket, approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-15, before review. Its components (payments.payments, payments.tests) cover payments.py and tests/test_approvals_remaining.py.
Mara Costa approved as code_review. She holds change_approver for payments and is a different person from the author, Aisha Bello.
The code_review approval names the head commit 6d48175a1230, so it covers what would be merged.

run.json shows CI ran on e6eb993, not head 6d48175. The later commit changes behaviour (the threshold comparison), so the run doesn't count. The JUnit report is also timestamped 2026-10-23 from a personal host, after the review time and inconsistent with the ci-runner-03 run.

Ledger entry ACR-0401, an exhaustive proof that required_approvals returns 2 iff a >= threshold, covers required_approvals, whose behaviour this change alters. That evidence lapses, and no new evidence of the same strength is provided; the old property is now false.
The change deviates from PAY-1, and the register has no approved, unexpired exception scoped to PAY-1 and payments.payments. The deviation is therefore not acceptable.

summary: The second commit, presented as a wording alignment, silently changes the dual-control comparison from >= to >. A payment of exactly 10,000.00 would then be releasable with a single approver, which violates PAY-1. No exception covers this deviation, and the existing exhaustive PAY-1 proof has lapsed with no replacement. The CI run is on the earlier commit, and its report timestamp and host are inconsistent with the recorded run, so testing on the final commit is not shown. The change is rejected.
